item.title: On the Divergence of Accuracy and Mechanism Consistency in Time Series World Models
item.description:
Authors: Haochen Zhang, Jiaheng Guo, Zhen Xu, Zachary Plotkin, Nicholas Konz, Zhen Tan, Tianlong Chen

A time series world model (TSWM) predicts a controlled system's state from its observed history and planned actions and exogenous inputs. Current approaches build forecasters with actions as covariates, trained and evaluated on prediction error under the executed plan. Yet world models compare unexecuted plans, but their responses to changed plans remain untested

- 方法：采用机器学习/深度学习模型。
- 任务：降尺度/预报/临近预测等应用场景。

item.title: Higher-Order Positional Encodings for Graph Representation Learning
item.description:
Authors: Caleb Stam, Aagrim Hoysal, Sanjukta Krishnagopal

Many real-world systems exhibit higher-order interactions among groups of entities that cannot be captured by pairwise relationships alone. Graph Transformers and Graph Neural Networks increasingly rely on positional encodings to enrich graph representations, yet existing positional encodings are computed solely from the original graph and therefore cannot directly capture observed higher-order interactions. item.description:

item.title: Weather-Aware Domain Adaptation for Street-View Weather Recognition
item.description:
Authors: Hossein Maghsoumi, George Atia, Yaser P. Fallah

Adverse conditions such as rain, snow, fog, and dust remain challenging for camera-based perception in autonomous driving. We study multi-class weather recognition from street-view images under domain shift, where most available training data come from non-street-view sources that differ markedly from real driving scenes. We propose Weather-Aware Adversarial Discriminative Domain Adaptation (WA-ADDA), which conditions the domain discriminator on predicted weather to promote features that are both domain-invariant and weather-sensitive

要点：
- 数据：包含再分析/卫星/观测等来源。

item.title: Foundations without Fundamentals: Zero-Shot Blind Spots in Time Series FMs
item.description:
Authors: Nafiseh Ghoroghchian, Haipeng Zhang, Shuyi Han, Alex Labach, George Stein

Despite the success of Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) on broad benchmarks, their ability to internalize basic temporal logic, especially in settings supported by exogenous covariates, remains under-examined. We introduce SimpleTimeBench, a diagnostic univariate and multivariate "unit test" suite for primitives such as monotonic trends, periodic signals and leading indicator covariates, scenarios where near-perfect forecasts should be trivial. Surprisingly, prominent multivariate TSFMs (Chronos-2, Moirai and Toto) frequently produce suboptimal zero-shot forecasts for these inputs

item.title: AI Emulation of Stochastic Sudden Stratospheric Warming with Interpretable Latent Structure
item.description:
Authors: C. Daniel Boscu, Daniel Hernandez, Fabio Alvarez Ventura, Justin Finkel, Ashesh Chattopadhyay, Pedram Hassanzadeh, Dorian S. Abbot

Rare weather regime transitions pose a challenge for data-driven modeling due to class imbalance. In this study, we develop a probabilistic deep learning emulator for a prototypical system with regime transitions, the stochastic Holton--Mass model of stratospheric variability, and analyze the structure of its learned latent space. item.title: A Comparative Explainability Framework for DeBERTa-v3 in Zero-Shot Medical Abstract Classification
item.description:
Authors: Javier Diaz Esteban-Herreros, David Muñoz-Valero, Raquel Martínez-España, Jose M. Juarez, Juan Moreno-Garcia

A comparative explainability framework is presented to audit DeBERTa-v3 under zero-shot classification of medical abstracts. The work addresses the disagreement problem in Explainable Artificial Intelligence, where different attribution methods produce divergent explanations for the same input and prediction. A natural language inference engine is implemented over the Medical Abstracts corpus with five enriched hypotheses per diagnostic category and a balanced sample of one thousand texts per class

item.title: Faynt: Scaling and Optimizing Policies for Competitive Melee
item.description:
Authors: Ali Janati, Nikita Kuzmin, Rohit Swamy, Charles Niu

After reinforcement learning (RL), the 10M wins 240 of 244 same-character games (98.4%) against fourteen specialist and multi-character releases on their supported rosters, with a winning record against every release

item.title: Decoding Looped Transformers Better for (Almost) Free
item.description:
Authors: Weihao Liu, Huangjie Zheng, Tianrong Chen, Rohit Dilip, Richard He Bai, Yizhu Jiao, Yuyang Wang, Ruixiang Zhang

Looped Transformers achieve parameter efficiency by repeatedly executing a shared block across recurrent loops. Each loop yields an intermediate representation decodable for the same next token, yet standard decoding discards earlier states. Because earlier loops embody less computation, recurrence inherently supplies aligned weak-and-strong prediction pairs without auxiliary models or external training
